text:
sarah: Heads-up: doing a nightly restore smoke on staging and noticed a couple of DB snapshot manifests with cleartext 'encryption_info' blocks inside the tar.
ben: do you mean the manifest file inside the snapshot or the S3 object metadata?
sarah: inside the tarball. path: s3://redwood-staging-restore/snap-2026-03-21-restore.tar.gz -> when I untarred, manifest.yaml includes:
```
encryption_info:
  method: none
  created_by: db-backup-agent-v0.9
```
ben: ugh. backup-agent v0.9 was supposed to be retired after RBAC rollouts. did we see any PutObject events from that agent yesterday?
auditor-alex: quick lookup in CloudTrail: there are PutObject events for principal backup-agent-v0.9 between 02:40-03:15 UTC. Most had sse: AES256 but metadata shows encryption_info.method none. looks like agent wrote metadata incorrectly while object payloads were SSE-KMS.
sarah: confirm: payloads are SSE-KMS (ServerSideEncryption: aws:kms) but manifest claims 'none' internally. that creates false negatives for our inventory scanner.
ops-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) update inventory scanner to detect manifest encryption_info.method mismatch with S3 SSE headers; 2) add a transient Lambda to scan recent uploads for manifests containing method:none and add tag remediation-required.
ben: agreed. I'll open a quick PR to inventory scanner to cross-check S3 head-object SSE header vs manifest encryption_info. Also will make the scanner flag severity=medium if manifest claims none but SSE is KMS.
auditor-alex: we should also run a retroactive query: find all PutObject events where object key matches "*manifest*" and the principal is backup-agent-v0.9 OR metadata contains encryption_info. Want a CSV of candidate objects and owners.
sarah: started exporting list to s3://redwood-audit-dumps/manifest-mismatch-2026-03-21.csv. dropping sample rows in the thread for context.
encops-bot: alert: manifest-internal-metadata-plaintext detected count=12 in buckets [redwood-staging-restore, redwood-archives] between 2026-03-20T23:00Z and 2026-03-21T04:00Z. Recommended action: run manifest-content-scan, run key-grant-audit for affected snapshots.
ben: two follow-ups: A) patch backup-agent to fail manifest write if it can't confirm envelope encryption (either SSE-KMS or client-side envelope), B) RBAC: remove write access from backup-agent-v0.9 immediately and rotate credentials.
ops-oncall: I've rotated the short-lived key for backup-agent-v0.9 and removed the role binding. I've left a rollback plan in INFSEC-1501 if failures occur.
auditor-alex: on scope: initial grep of object contents shows manifests only list snapshot metadata and pointer URLs, no DB credentials or encryption keys. still: a compliance finding because manifests could leak topology. mark as compliance-low unless content includes secrets.
sarah: thanks. putting a note in INFSEC-1501: customer-impact=false for now, follow-up inventory needed.
ben: also verifying KMS grants: run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <cmk>` for CMKs used by archives/staging to see if any grants were issued to legacy principals. I found one stale grant to arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-agent-v0.9-grant. will schedule revoke after cross-check.
encops-bot: runbook reminder: if any manifest contains full table schemas or backup tokens then escalate to P1.
sarah: next steps: 1) complete inventory scan (ben), 2) patch agent (ben), 3) revoke stale grants and rotate creds (ops-oncall), 4) add S3 bucket policy to reject PutObject where object metadata/encryption_info="none" (auditor-alex to propose policy), 5) customer comms only if manifests include sensitive payloads (sarah).
ben: tagging INFSEC-1501 and assigning owners. I'll post PR link when ready.
ops-oncall: ping me if any restore jobs start failing after RBAC removal. I'll be standing by. :white_check_mark:
